chapters.title: The Word Became Flesh
chapters.html:
John 1

The Word

1In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

2He was in the beginning with God.

3All things came into being through Him, and without Him not one thing came into being.

4What has come into being in Him was life, and the life was the light of mankind.

5The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.

6There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.

7He came as a witness, to bear witness about the light, so that all might believe through him.

8He was not the light, but came to bear witness about the light.

9The true light, which gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.

10He was in the world, and the world came into being through Him, yet the world did not know Him.

11He came to His own, and His own people did not receive Him.

12But to all who received Him, who believe in His name, He gave the right to become children of God,

13who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.

14The Word became flesh and pitched His tent among us, and we have seen His glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.

15(John bore witness about Him and cried out, "This was He of whom I said, 'He who comes after me has gone ahead of me, because He was before me.'")

16For from His fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.

17For the Law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

18No one has ever seen God; the only Son, who is God, who is at the Father's side, He has made Him known.

The Witness of John

19This is the witness of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"

20He confessed, and did not deny; he confessed, "I am not the Messiah."

21They asked him, "What then? Are you Elijah?" He said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" He answered, "No."

22So they said to him, "Who are you? Let us give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"

23He said, "I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, 'Make straight the way of the Lord,' as Isaiah the prophet said."

24They had been sent from the Pharisees.

25They asked him, "Then why are you baptizing, if you are not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"

26John answered them, "I baptize with water; among you stands one whom you do not know,

27He who comes after me, the strap of whose sandal I am not worthy to untie."

28This took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

The Lamb of God

29The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him, and said, "Look: the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!

30This is He of whom I said, 'After me comes a man who has gone ahead of me, because He was before me.'

31I myself did not know Him; but I came baptizing with water for this, that He might be revealed to Israel."

32John bore witness, saying, "I saw the Spirit coming down from heaven like a dove, and it remained on Him.

33I myself did not know Him; but the One who sent me to baptize with water said to me, 'The one on whom you see the Spirit come down and remain, this is He who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'

34I have seen, and have borne witness that this is the Chosen One of God."

The First Disciples

35The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples,

36and he looked at Jesus as He walked by and said, "Look: the Lamb of God!"

37The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.

38Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, "What are you looking for?" They said to Him, "Rabbi" (which translated means Teacher), "where are You staying?"

39He said to them, "Come and you will see." So they came and saw where He was staying, and they stayed with Him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

40One of the two who heard John and followed Him was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.

41He first found his own brother Simon and said to him, "We have found the Messiah" (which translated means Christ).

42He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon the son of John. You will be called Cephas" (which is translated Peter).

43The next day He decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip, and Jesus said to him, "Follow Me."

44Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.

45Philip found Nathanael and said to him, "We have found Him of whom Moses in the Law, and also the prophets, wrote: Jesus son of Joseph, from Nazareth."

46Nathanael said to him, "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?" Philip said to him, "Come and see."

47Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward Him and said of him, "Here truly is an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!"

48Nathanael said to Him, "How do You know me?" Jesus answered him, "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."

49Nathanael answered Him, "Rabbi, You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"

50Jesus answered him, "Because I said to you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these."

51He said to him, "Truly, truly, I tell you all, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" — En archē, in the beginning, is letter for letter how the Greek of Genesis opens, En archē epoiēsen ho theos, In the beginning, God created (Genesis 1:1). Logos, Word: Greek had a plain word for something said, rhēma, and John does not use it. Logos is from legō, to gather or lay in order; it came to mean an account, a reckoning, the reason or ordering principle of a thing. The scriptures had already said By the word of the LORD the heavens were made (Psalm 33:6), and Wisdom, who made all things by Your word (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). Pros ton theon, with God, word for word toward God, face to face. Theos ēn ho logos: theos set first for weight and without the article, the Word was God; in the line before, with the article, ton theon, God whom the Word was with.

  • vv3–5 "All things came into being through Him… What has come into being in Him was life… the darkness has not overcome it" — egeneto, came into being, set against ēn, was: the Word was, all else came to be. The edition puts ho gegonen, what has come into being, at the start of the sentence of v4; the verse numbers put it at the end of v3, which reads not one thing came into being that has come into being. The light shining in darkness is the first day, "Light — be." And light was (Genesis 1:3). Katelaben, has overcome, also means has grasped, laid hold of with the hand or the mind.

  • vv6–13 "a man sent from God… The true light… was coming into the world… the right to become children of God" — John the Baptist is never called the Baptist in this book. Erchomenon, coming, may go with the light or with everyone, every person coming into the world. Ta idia… hoi idioi, His own… His own people: first His own things, His home, then His own people. Ex haimatōn, of blood, plural in Greek, of bloods.

  • v14 "The Word became flesh and pitched His tent among us… the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth" — eskēnōsen, pitched His tent, from skēnē, the tent of meeting where the glory of the LORD filled the dwelling (Exodus 40:34). Wisdom says in Sirach, Pitch your tent in Jacob (Sirach 24:8), with the same verb in Greek. Monogenēs, only, the one of its kind, as the widow's only son (Luke 7:12). Grace and truth is the LORD's name before Moses, abundant in loyal love and truth (Exodus 34:6).

  • vv15–17 "He was before me… grace upon grace… the Law was given through Moses" — prōtos mou, before me, word for word first of me: John was born first, but the Word was first. Charin anti charitos, grace upon grace, word for word grace in place of grace: one grace given after another, or the grace of Christ in place of the grace of the Law.

  • v18 "No one has ever seen God; the only Son, who is God… at the Father's side" — You cannot see My face, because no human being can see Me and live (Exodus 33:20). The edition reads monogenēs theos, word for word only God, and marks it as a place where manuscripts differ. Eis ton kolpon, at the Father's side, word for word into the bosom, as Lazarus at Abraham's side (Luke 16:22). Exēgēsato, He has made Him known, laid Him out, the root of exegesis.

  • vv19–28 "the Jews… Are you Elijah?… the Prophet?… the voice of one crying out in the wilderness" — hoi Ioudaioi, the Jews, here the ones in Jerusalem who send priests and Levites. Elijah was promised before the great and fearful day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5); the Prophet is the one Moses foretold, A prophet… like me (Deuteronomy 18:15). The voice is Isaiah's, In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD (Isaiah 40:3), with Make straight from its next line.

  • vv29–34 "the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world… the Spirit… remained on Him… the Chosen One of God" — Abraham said, God will see to the lamb for a burnt offering (Genesis 22:8), and the servant goes like a lamb that is led to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7). Menon, remain, the word this book uses of abiding (vv38–39). The edition reads ho eklektos, the Chosen One, as Isaiah's My chosen one… I have put My Spirit on him (Isaiah 42:1), and marks it as a place where manuscripts differ; others have the Son of God.

  • vv35–42 "What are you looking for?… where are You staying?… Come and you will see… Cephas" — the first words of Jesus in this book are a question. Menō, stay, three times in vv38–39. The tenth hour, counted from sunrise, late afternoon. Kēphas is Aramaic for rock, as Petros is Greek; Matthew has you are Peter, and on this rock (Matthew 16:18).

  • vv43–51 "an Israelite in whom there is no deceit… under the fig tree… the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man" — Jacob, who became Israel, came to his father with deceit (Genesis 27:35); the Greek has dolos there and here. Blessed is the man… in whose spirit there is no deceit (Psalm 32:2). Jacob's dream at Bethel: a stairway was set on the earth… Messengers of God were going up and coming down on it (Genesis 28:12); here the Son of Man is the stairway. Amēn amēn, truly, truly, doubled only in this book. Hymin, you all, plural.

chapters.title: Water into Wine
chapters.html:
John 2

The Wedding at Cana

1On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.

2Jesus also was invited to the wedding, with His disciples.

3When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to Him, "They have no wine."

4Jesus said to her, "Woman, what is that to you and to Me? My hour has not yet come."

5His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever He tells you."

6Six stone water jars were standing there for the Jewish rites of purification, each holding two or three measures.

7Jesus said to them, "Fill the jars with water." They filled them up to the brim.

8He said to them, "Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast." So they took it.

9When the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from — though the servants who had drawn the water knew — the master of the feast called the bridegroom

10and said to him, "Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, the poorer wine. You have kept the good wine until now."

11This, the first of His signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and revealed His glory; and His disciples believed in Him.

12After this He went down to Capernaum, with His mother and His brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.

The Temple Cleared

13The Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

14In the temple He found those who were selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money changers sitting there.

15He made a whip of cords and drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and the oxen. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables,

16and to those who sold the doves He said, "Take these things away from here! Do not make My Father's house a house of trade."

17His disciples remembered that it is written, "Zeal for Your house will consume Me."

18So the Jews answered Him, "What sign do You show us, since You do these things?"

19Jesus answered them, "Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it up."

20The Jews then said, "This sanctuary was built in forty-six years, and You will raise it up in three days?"

21But He was speaking about the sanctuary of His body.

22So when He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

23While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in His name when they saw the signs He was doing.

24But Jesus Himself did not entrust Himself to them, because He knew all people,

25and He had no need for anyone to bear witness about man, for He Himself knew what was in man.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "On the third day there was a wedding at Cana" — counted from the last day of chapter 1. Kana, a village of Galilee, named in the Bible only in this book (again in 4:46 and 21:2).

  • vv3–5 "Woman, what is that to you and to Me? My hour has not yet come… Do whatever He tells you" — gynai, woman, is not cold in Greek; Jesus says it to His mother again from the cross (19:26). Ti emoi kai soi, word for word what to Me and to you?, the words of the widow to Elijah, What have I to do with you, man of God? (1 Kings 17:18): what is between us in this? Hē hōra mou, My hour, the hour Jesus later says has come for the Son of Man to be glorified (12:23). Whatever He tells you is Pharaoh's word to Egypt, Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do (Genesis 41:55).

  • vv6–10 "Six stone water jars… for the Jewish rites of purification… You have kept the good wine until now" — Metrētēs, measure, a liquid measure. Architriklinos, master of the feast, the guest in charge of the table. The water kept for washing becomes the wine of the wedding; the prophets saw the last days with aged wine well refined (Isaiah 25:6) and the mountains will drip sweet wine (Amos 9:13).

  • v11 "the first of His signs… revealed His glory" — archē tōn sēmeiōn, the first of the signs, word for word the beginning of the signs, with the archē of 1:1. Sēmeion, sign, this book's word for His miracles: each points to who He is. The glory is the one we have seen (1:14).

  • vv13–17 "the Passover of the Jews… a whip of cords… My Father's house a house of trade… Zeal for Your house will consume Me" — the other Gospels put this at the end of His work, after the entry into Jerusalem (Mark 11:15); John puts it at the start. Oikon emporiou, a house of trade: there will no longer be a Canaanite, a trader, in the house of the LORD of hosts (Zechariah 14:21). The Psalm, zeal for Your house has consumed me (Psalm 69:9); John has the future, will consume, as the Greek of the Psalm does.

  • vv18–22 "Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it up… forty-six years… the sanctuary of His body" — naos, sanctuary, the house itself, where hieron, temple (vv14–15), is the whole precinct. At His trial the charge was I will destroy this sanctuary made with hands (Mark 14:58); here He says Destroy, and the destroying is theirs. Egerō, I will raise, the verb used of His rising (v22).

  • vv23–25 "many believed in His name… Jesus Himself did not entrust Himself to them" — episteusan… ouk episteuen, believed… did not entrust, the same verb: they put their trust in Him, but He did not put His in them. He knew what was in man, as the LORD looks at the heart (1 Samuel 16:7).
